title_en: Currency Hedging & Navigating Global Markets Through ETFs
title_zh: Maria Ronnie 与 Sandra Testani：货币对冲与借 ETF 穿越全球市场
subtitle_zh: 拆解 HFXI 的 50% 货币对冲逻辑，并盘点 American Century 的 ETF 增长与市场观点。
description: Currency Hedging & Navigating Global Markets Through ETFs

turns.en: We like to call it the hedge of least regret. All right, joining me will be Maria Ronnie, senior director, equities product manager at New York Life Investments, who currently offers 21 ETFs, over $8 billion in assets.
turns.zh: 我们喜欢管它叫'最不后悔的对冲'（hedge of least regret）。好，今天加入我的是 Maria Ronnie，New York Life Investments 的董事总经理（senior director）兼股票产品经理，该公司目前提供 21 只 ETF，资产超过 80 亿美元。

turns.en: And I'll tell you, sometimes an ETF just catches my attention for whatever reason. It could be flows, performance, the strategy itself. There are a number of reasons.
turns.zh: 我跟你说，有时候某只 ETF 就是因为各种原因引起我的注意。可能是资金流、业绩、或者策略本身。原因有很多。

turns.en: And as I was looking at the New York Life lineup, I noticed the most popular ETF by assets is the FTSE International Equity Currency Neutral ETF, ticker HFXI, which just has over $2 billion invested in it.
turns.zh: 我看 New York Life 的产品线时注意到，按资产算最受欢迎的是 FTSE International Equity Currency Neutral ETF，代码 HFXI，里面的投资已经超过 20 亿美元。

turns.en: It's taken in nearly $800 million just this year. So that certainly caught my attention. And then if you look at performance, it's actually outperformed a number of the largest developed international ETFs, in large part, because it does have this currency hedging component.
turns.zh: 仅今年一年它就吸进了将近 8 亿美元。所以这确实引起了我的注意。再看业绩，它实际上跑赢了不少规模最大的发达市场国际 ETF，很大程度上就是因为它有这个货币对冲（currency hedging）部分。

turns.en: And if you think about that, with all of the headlines around the strength of the US dollar or lack thereof, there's a lot of debate around that right now. And so I would say the bottom line is this ETF checks a lot of boxes of intrigue for me.
turns.zh: 你想想看，现在到处都是关于美元强弱、或者谈不上强弱的头条，眼下围绕这个话题的争论很多。所以我想说，底线是：这只 ETF 在我眼里勾起了很多好奇心的点。

turns.en: And so Maria and I are going to dive fairly deeply into this ETF, I would say particularly around that currency hedging component. And then along with that, we'll have a conversation around the current state of international stocks overall, which of course have been outperforming for a while now, going back to the beginning of last year.
turns.zh: 所以 Maria 和我会相当深入地聊这只 ETF，我说的重点是那个货币对冲的部分。除此之外，我们也会聊聊当前国际股票的整体状况，当然它们已经跑赢一段时间了，从去年年初就开始了。

turns.en: So we'll discuss some key considerations for investors. Now, later, I'll be joined by Sandra Testani, head of Global ETF Product and Strategy at American Century, who they continue to move up the ETF leaderboard, currently 49 ETFs and all, about $160 billion in assets.
turns.zh: 我们会讨论投资者需要考虑的几个要点。稍后，American Century 全球 ETF 产品与策略主管 Sandra Testani 会加入我，他们一直在 ETF 排行榜上往上走，目前 49 只 ETF，资产总计约 1,600 亿美元。

turns.en: Of course, that includes both American Century branded ETFs, along with the Avantus ETF lineup. And so Sandra's going to give us the latest on that growth and the positioning of their ETF lineup overall.
turns.zh: 当然，这既包括 American Century 自有品牌的 ETF，也包括 Avantus 的 ETF 产品线。所以 Sandra 会告诉我们这些增长的最新情况，以及他们 ETF 产品线的整体定位。

turns.en: And then from there, we're going to take a nice tour through the financial markets, talking US stocks, international stocks, fixed income, Sandra's an excellent market and ETF resource.
turns.zh: 然后从那里出发，我们要沿着金融市场好好转一圈，聊聊美国股票、国际股票、固定收益。Sandra 是很出色的市场和 ETF 资源。

turns.en: So we'll find out how she's viewing everything at the moment and highlight a few American Century ETFs along the way. As always, questions or comments, you can find me on X at Nate Geracy, or you can go to etfprime.com.
turns.zh: 所以我们来听听她此刻如何看待一切，途中也会重点介绍几只 American Century 的 ETF。像往常一样，有问题或评论，可以在 X 上找我，Nate Geraci，或者访问 etfprime.com。

turns.en: So let me first welcome in Maria Rani, again, senior director, equities product manager with New York Life Investments. Maria, it is a pleasure.
turns.zh: 那么我先欢迎 Maria Ronnie，再次说明，她是 New York Life Investments 的董事总经理兼股票产品经理。Maria，非常高兴。

turns.en: Welcome to the podcast. Hi, Nate. Thanks for having me on. All right. So as I mentioned, we are going to focus on HFXI, but as I was looking at flows into your lineup overall, that's not the only ETF that's been attracting attention, right?
turns.zh: 欢迎上节目。嗨，Nate，谢谢邀请。好，正如我提到的，我们会聚焦 HFXI，但我看你整条产品线的资金流入时，它并不是唯一吸引注意力的 ETF，对吧？

turns.en: As it turns out, I'm showing all but three of your 21 ETFs have taken a new money this year, which is obviously pretty darn good. So just tell us what's been going on with New York Life ETFs overall.
turns.zh: 事实上，我这边显示，你那 21 只 ETF 里除了 3 只，今年全都获得了新钱，这显然相当漂亮。那就跟我们说说 New York Life 的 ETF 整体情况如何。

turns.en: Yeah, our ETF business has obviously been a huge focus for us, as with many other firms, we've been lucky to see an acceleration of flows over the last year and year to date as well.
turns.zh: 是的，我们的 ETF 业务显然一直是我们的重心，跟许多其他公司一样，我们很幸运在过去一年以及今年都看到资金流明显加速。

turns.en: We now have three ETFs with over a billion dollars in assets, which is really exciting. The top flowing ETFs are HFXI, obviously, that you mentioned.
turns.zh: 我们现在有三只资产超过 10 亿美元的 ETF，这真的令人振奋。流入最多的就是 HFXI，显然就是你提到的那一只。

turns.en: That's our passive international strategy. We also have two active municipal bond strategies, MMIT, which is an intermediate muni strategy and MMIN, which is an insured active muni bond strategy.
turns.zh: 那是我们的被动的国际策略。我们还有两只主动管理的市政债（municipal bond）策略，MMIT 是一只中等久期的市政债策略，MMIN 是一只带保险（insured）的主动市政债策略。

turns.en: So we've seen some interest in those as well. We also have a passive systematic hedge fund replication strategy. The ticker on that is QAI. It's actually been exciting.
turns.zh: 所以我们也看到对这些产品的兴趣。我们还有一只被动的系统性对冲基金复制策略，代码是 QAI。它其实也挺让人兴奋的。

turns.en: We've been seeing some institutional interest there. So nice to see that there's an appetite for that kind of strategy in that market. If you had to summarize how New York Life is positioned within the ETF marketplace, how would you describe that?
turns.zh: 我们在那里看到了一些机构层面的兴趣。所以很高兴看到这类策略在这个市场里有需求。如果要你概括 New York Life 在 ETF 市场中的定位，你会怎么描述？

turns.en: Like what do you lead with when you're first having conversations with clients around your lineup? Yeah, well, just like in our mutual fund business, we're a multi-boutique structure. So our goal is to work with, and we work with a number of affiliated and unaffiliated sub-advisors to launch active ETFs.
turns.zh: 比如，当你第一次和客户聊起你的产品线时，你最先讲的是什么？嗯，就像我们的共同基金业务一样，我们是多精品（multi-boutique）结构。所以我们的目标是与许多关联和关联外的子顾问（sub-advisors）合作，推出主动 ETF。

turns.en: That's been our focus from a product development perspective is to boost our active ETF lineup. So our goal is to work with experts in their respective fields to launch those strategies in different market segments.
turns.zh: 从产品开发的角度看，我们的重心一直是壮大主动 ETF 产品线。所以我们的目标是与各领域的专家合作，在不同的细分市场推出这些策略。

turns.en: So for example, we have a couple of large cap growth equity ETFs, a municipal bond suite, a couple that I mentioned already. We have a taxable bond suite as well.
turns.zh: 举例来说，我们有几只大盘成长股票 ETF，一套市政债产品线，我刚才已经提到两只。我们也有一套应税债券产品线。

turns.en: That includes a core plus, high yield and securitized bond strategies. We also have specialty equity strategies and we also recently launched an international SMID strategy with our affiliate out in Australia.
turns.zh: 其中包括核心加（core plus）、高收益和资产证券化（securitized）债券策略。我们还有特色股票策略，最近还和我们在澳大利亚的关联公司一起推出了一只国际中小盘（SMID）策略。

turns.en: So that's very exciting. We also have a couple of passive strategies that have been out a little bit longer. Obviously, HFXI is one of them.
turns.zh: 所以那非常令人兴奋。我们还有几只存在时间更长一些的策略。显然，HFXI 是其中之一。

turns.en: QAI is one of them. We also have another systematic liquid alternatives ETF. It's a merger arbitrage strategy, M&A, and both of those were launched in 2009.
turns.zh: QAI 也是其中之一。我们还有一只系统性流动替代（liquid alternatives）ETF，是一个并购套利（merger arbitrage）策略，代码 M&A，这两只都是在 2009 年成立的。

turns.en: So those have quite a bit of track record there as well. And I'm assuming you're going to tell me that everybody is a potential investor, but do you tend to work more with financial advisors or who is the prototypical buyer of New York Life ETFs?
turns.zh: 所以它们的业绩记录也挺长。我猜你接下来会告诉我，每个人都是潜在投资者，但你们是不是更多和财务顾问打交道，还是说 New York Life ETF 的典型买家是谁？

turns.en: Typically, yes. We work with a lot of retail advisors. There is more interest to expand more into institutional as well, but definitely our focus has been on the retail side.
turns.zh: 通常确实如此。我们和很多零售顾问合作。向机构端扩展的兴趣在增加，但我们的重心肯定一直在零售侧。

turns.en: Okay. So as I noted at the top, I was perusing your ETF lineup and HFXI just jumped off the page to me. So again, this is the New York Life FTSE international equity currency, neutral ETF.
turns.zh: 好。就像我开头说的，我在翻看你的 ETF 产品线时，HFXI 直接跳到了我眼前。再说一次，这是 New York Life FTSE 国际股票货币中性 ETF。

turns.en: I noted this now has over $2 billion in assets, including that nearly 800 million in inflows this year. And of course, the US dollar and international stocks are in the headlines right now, which I think makes this ETF very timely.
turns.zh: 我注意到它现在的资产超过 20 亿美元，其中包括今年将近 8 亿美元的流入。当然，美元和国际股票现在都在头条上，我觉得这让这只 ETF 非常应景。

turns.en: I guess first, do you want to walk us through the basic strategy here? You noted this is obviously index based, but take us from there. Yeah, absolutely.
turns.zh: 我想首先，你要不要带我们走一遍这里的基本策略？你也提到了这显然是指数化的，那就从这里往下讲。嗯，当然。

turns.en: So as I mentioned, this has a long track record. We launched it 11 years ago. It is passive. It tracks a FTSE index. It's the FTSE developed X North America 50% hedged index.
turns.zh: 正如我说的，它有很长的业绩记录。我们 11 年前推出了它。它是被动的，跟踪一个 FTSE 指数，即 FTSE 发达市场不含北美 50% 对冲指数（FTSE Developed ex North America 50% Hedged Index）。

turns.en: So it's market cap weighted. It's very simple. It's broad, diversified, developed exposure, basically an equity beta, right? But the main differentiator is, as you mentioned, we hedge 50% of the currency exposure.
turns.zh: 所以它是市值加权的。非常简单，是广泛分散的发达市场敞口，基本上就是股票 beta，对吧？但主要的差异点，就像你说的，我们对冲 50% 的货币敞口。

turns.en: So it's basically this currency neutral overlay embedded into the portfolio. There's 14 different currencies within the portfolio that we have exposure to.
turns.zh: 所以本质上这是嵌在组合里的一个货币中性（currency neutral）叠加层。我们的组合里有 14 种不同的货币敞口。

turns.en: So each of those is 50% hedged. And we reset the hedge on a monthly basis to keep that 50% hedge consistent over time. Talk more about this currency hedging component, because clearly this is the differentiator here.
turns.zh: 每一种都是 50% 对冲。我们每月重置对冲，以便长期保持这个 50% 的对冲比例。多讲讲这个货币对冲的部分，因为这显然是这里的差异点。

turns.en: And the whole idea is, I think about this, is you're sort of straddling the line, right? You're avoiding making a full bet for against the US dollar.
turns.zh: 而整个思路，我是这么想的，就是你相当于骑在中间线上，对吧？你避免就对美元做一个全面的下注或押反。

turns.en: So you are 50% hedge, 50% unhedged. Why do you think that's potentially a better way to go? Well, currency hedging lowers volatility. And the great thing about that is that, you know, you're allowed, you're able to be kind of in the middle and not make a currency call.
turns.zh: 所以你是 50% 对冲、50% 不对冲。你为什么觉得这可能是更好的走法？嗯，货币对冲会降低波动率。而它的好处在于，你可以待在中间位置，而不用做货币判断。

turns.en: So in the market, if you look at kind of the ETF landscape for international, you have unhedged and you have fully hedged 100% hedge that 100% hedged.
turns.zh: 所以在市场上，你看看国际类 ETF 的格局，要么是不对冲，要么是完全对冲、100% 对冲。

turns.en: Yes, it's going to lower volatility, but you're also making a currency call. You are betting on the dollar, you're bullish on the dollar. On the other hand, if you're unhedged, you're bullish on the foreign currencies versus the dollar.
turns.zh: 是的，100% 对冲会降低波动率，但你同时也做了一个货币判断。你在押注美元、你看好美元。另一方面，如果你不对冲，那就是你看好外币相对美元。

turns.en: So if someone has, you know, a high conviction on currencies and that's their prerogative and they want to invest in one or the other, that's fine.
turns.zh: 所以如果有人对货币有很高的确信，那是他们的选择，他们想投哪一种都可以，这没问题。

turns.en: But of course, you know, many investors believe that it can add undue risk to a portfolio. So if an investor does not have high conviction one way or the other, they may want to consider that partial hedge instead.
turns.zh: 但当然，很多投资者认为这会给组合带来不必要的风险。所以如果投资者对某一边没有高确信，他们可能要考虑这个部分对冲。

turns.en: We like to call it the hedge of least regret. It allows an investor to kind of split that difference and not make the currency call, but still mitigate some of that currency risk.
turns.zh: 我们喜欢称之为'最不后悔的对冲'。它让投资者能够折中，不做货币判断，但仍然缓解掉一部分货币风险。

turns.en: And what we've seen is that the half hedge can help manage that volatility. It can help reduce downside capture. And, you know, we've also seen competitive returns over time as a result.
turns.zh: 我们看到的是，半对冲可以帮助管理那个波动率，可以帮助降低下行捕获（downside capture）。而且因此我们也看到了长期具有竞争力的回报。

turns.en: To your point on volatility, it's interesting. I've seen a number of white papers that, to exactly what you're saying, they say currencies essentially just add volatility to a portfolio.
turns.zh: 关于你说的波动率这点很有意思。我见过不少白皮书，正如你所说，它们认为货币本质上只是给组合增加了波动率。

turns.en: And so you'll see some asset managers out there, ones who are offering 100% hedging, that they say, well, that's why you should put on 100% hedge is because you're going to lower that volatility.
turns.zh: 所以你会看到一些做 100% 对冲的资产管理人说，这就是为什么你应该上 100% 对冲，因为那会降低波动率。

turns.en: But it sounds like you're saying either way, you're still making a bet there. You have to have conviction on the currency. Right. And, you know, again, yes, it is going to lower volatility, but if you're in an environment like last year where the dollar is down 10%, that's not going to work for you if you're 100% hedged.
turns.zh: 但听起来你的意思是，无论哪种做法，你其实仍然在下注。你必须对货币有确信。对。而且再说一次，是的，它确实会降低波动率，但如果像去年那样美元下跌 10% 的环境，100% 对冲对你就不管用。

turns.en: At least if you're 50% hedge, it helps kind of soften that blow. But then if the dollar does strengthen, you're able to at least take part in some of that appreciation.
turns.zh: 至少如果你是 50% 对冲，它有助于缓解那一击。而如果美元确实走强，你至少也能分享到一部分升值。

turns.en: And we don't have to get fully into the weeds here, but I do always like to cover the basics on this podcast. So do you mind explaining just how is that 50% currency heads actually put on?
turns.zh: 我们不必挖到最深，但我在这个节目上一直喜欢把基础问题讲清楚。你介意解释一下，那 50% 的货币对冲到底是怎么搭上去的？

turns.en: And are there any additional costs involved with that? We, you know, create the hedge and we utilize currency forward contracts to implement the hedge.
turns.zh: 这里面有什么额外成本吗？我们，你知道，构建对冲时使用的是货币远期合约（currency forward contracts）来实施对冲。

turns.en: Pretty simple. Um, in terms of the costs, it's really based on interest rate differentials. So under current market market conditions, uh, with US rates being higher than international rates, there's actually been a positive carry associated with implementing that hedge.
turns.zh: 相当简单。成本方面，实际上取决于利差（interest rate differentials）。所以在当前市场环境下，美国利率高于国际利率，实施那个对冲反而带来了正的持有收益（positive carry）。

turns.en: Obviously this can fluctuate over time and we don't, you know, say that this is a meaningful source of return. Um, obviously this could change if we see rates increase overseas.
turns.zh: 显然这会随时间波动，我们也不认为这是收益的一个重要来源。显然，如果海外利率上升，这个情况可能会改变。

turns.en: Yeah. And I should note the expense ratio on this, uh, ETF is a 20 basis points. Obviously very competitive given the currency hedging component.
turns.zh: 是。我还应该说明一下，这只 ETF 的费率是 20 个基点。考虑到有货币对冲这一部分，显然非常有竞争力。

turns.en: Um, how are you seeing this ETF being used in a portfolio? Like, is this a full replacement for unhedged international exposure or compliment?
turns.zh: 你看到这个 ETF 在组合中是怎么被使用的？比如，它是完全替代不对冲的国际敞口，还是补充？

turns.en: How do you typically see advisors utilizing this ETF? Yeah. I mean, we believe it could be a replacement for an unhedged strategy because again, you're kind of straddling that line.
turns.zh: 你通常看到顾问怎么用这只 ETF？嗯，我们认为它可以替代一个不对冲的策略，因为再说一次，你相当于骑在那条线中间。

turns.en: Um, and from an equity perspective, it gives you that broad diversified exposure. So it's passive from an equity perspective, but it also has that passive currency edge as well.
turns.zh: 而且从股票角度看，它给你广泛分散的敞口。所以从股票角度它是被动的，但同时也带着那个被动式的货币优势。

turns.en: So you don't have any active equity or currency bets happening in the portfolio. Um, so we believe it can be a core holding and an international sleeve.
turns.zh: 所以组合里既没有主动的股票押注，也没有货币押注。我们认为它可以作为国际部分（international sleeve）里的核心持仓。

turns.en: Um, and even compliment more, you know, higher active, uh, conviction strategies. Okay. So let's talk more about the current market environment.
turns.zh: 甚至可以补充那些更高确信度的主动策略。好，那我们多聊聊当前的市场环境。

turns.en: And obviously we're not here to make any market calls. You don't have a crystal ball. It's been very well documented that my crystal ball is completely shattered.
turns.zh: 显然我们不是来做市场预测的。你也没有水晶球。而且我那个水晶球彻底碎了这件事已经众所周知了。

turns.en: Um, however, I would love your thoughts around the US dollar right now. And I get the point of HFXI is that you don't have to make any sort of call on the dollar.
turns.zh: 不过，我很想听听你对眼下美元的思考。我也明白 HFXI 的意义就在于，你不非得对美元做任何判断。

turns.en: However, investors do have to consider whether they want this 50% hedge. And so like, what are you thinking about as you look at the US dollar right now?
turns.zh: 但投资者确实要考虑自己是否想要这个 50% 对冲。所以，你看着眼下的美元时，你在想些什么？

turns.en: Well, so our global market strategy team here at Nilem, um, that's our team of economists. They believe that partially hedging and international right now for US investors, uh, does make sense right now.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们 NYLIM 的全球市场策略团队，那是我们的经济学家团队，他们认为，对美国投资者来说，现在对国际资产做部分对冲是有道理的。

turns.en: Um, you know, the dollar is a key safe haven asset. So in periods of time where there's heightened geopolitical risk, like we're seeing right now with the conflict in Iran, um, we see a flight to safety, which is supportive of the dollar.
turns.zh: 美元是关键的避险资产。所以在地缘政治风险升高的时期，比如我们现在看到的伊朗冲突，我们会看到避险资金流入，这对美元是支撑。

turns.en: And we've seen that so far this year. Um, but again, you know, it's important to remember that currencies can be volatile. They're difficult to predict their direction.
turns.zh: 今年到目前为止我们也看到了这一点。但同样，重要的是要记住货币可能很波动，它们的方向很难预测。

turns.en: Uh, you know, even in the last year and a half, there's been quite a bit of volatility in the dollar, as I mentioned last year. And then we see, we saw a pickup this year and then a little bit of a downturn more recently.
turns.zh: 你知道，即便在过去一年半里，美元已经相当波动，正如我提到的去年。然后我们看到今年有起色，最近又有点回落。

turns.en: Um, but over the long term, you know, if you look 20 plus years, the average annual impact of currencies to returns internationally has been about plus or minus five, uh, 6%, um, which is significant.
turns.zh: 但从长期看，如果你看 20 多年的数据，货币对国际投资回报的平均年度影响大约是正负 5%、6%，这是相当显著的。

turns.en: And especially if you don't know if that's going to detract or add to your returns over time. So that partial hedge can really help lower that volatility and smooth the returns out over time.
turns.zh: 尤其是当你不知道它长期是会拖累还是会增加你的回报时。所以那个部分对冲真的有助于降低波动率，并让长期回报更平滑。

turns.en: Well, and you make an interesting point because obviously there are periods of time where you do see this flight to safety and clearly the dollar is the global reserve currency.
turns.zh: 你提了一个有意思的点，因为显然有些时期你会看到这种避险流入，而且美元显然是全球储备货币。

turns.en: That's where people will go. But at the same time, and we've seen this more recently, there are a lot of concerns around the, uh, the, the rising government debt.
turns.zh: 资金就会流向那里。但与此同时，我们最近也看到了这一点，围绕政府债务不断上升有很多担忧。

turns.en: And, you know, we saw this intervention in the treasury market and those sorts of things can weigh on the dollar. And so you have, as an investor, you're sitting here looking at these different, um, you know, this, this give and take on the dollar.
turns.zh: 我们看到了国债市场上的那种干预，这类事情会对美元形成压力。所以作为投资者，你坐在这里看着关于美元的这些此消彼长。

turns.en: And it can be difficult to your point to make a prediction on where it's going to go. Um, what about international stocks more broadly? So I mentioned the outperformance earlier, you know, that goes back to about the beginning of last year.
turns.zh: 正如你所说，要预测它的走向可能很难。那么更宽泛地看国际股票呢？我前面提到了那个跑赢，大概可以追溯到去年年初。

turns.en: And if I look at HFXI specifically, this is as of this morning, it's up 54% versus 33% on the S and P 500. That's since January 2025. So how, how are you viewing that outperformance?
turns.zh: 如果具体看 HFXI，这是截至今天早上的数据，它涨了 54%，而标普 500（S&P 500）是 33%，那是从 2025 年 1 月以来算的。所以你怎么看这种跑赢？

turns.en: Yeah. So our global market strategy team is looking at a few key themes. Um, you know, first in Europe, you see Germany began a wave of countries, you know, increasing their defense and infrastructure spending, which has subsequently seen a bump in private sector spending come in as well.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们的全球市场策略团队在看几个关键主题。首先，在欧洲，你看到德国开启了一波国家增加国防和基础设施开支的浪潮，随之而来的是私营部门的支出也跟了上来。

turns.en: And it's resulted in resilient bank lending activity. Even with the ECB in the midst of a hiking cycle. Um, so we've seen European financials benefit from this pickup and activity over in Japan, there's been strong corporate reform activity and it's been driving improvements in return on equity.
turns.zh: 这带来了有韧性的银行放贷活动。即便欧洲央行（ECB）正处于加息周期之中。所以我们看到欧洲金融股受益于那边活动的回升。在日本，企业改革活动很强，它正在推动股东权益回报率（ROE）的改善。

turns.en: Um, even equity listing requirements have changed to encourage the deployment of cash by large companies as opposed to just hoarding that cash.
turns.zh: 甚至股票上市要求也发生了变化，以鼓励大公司把现金投放出去，而不只是囤积现金。

turns.en: So obviously that's going to be a positive for growth prospects, uh, in the country. Uh, again, these are just a couple of the themes that our team is watching right now, uh, overseas and why they still have conviction in international equities.
turns.zh: 所以那显然对该国的增长前景是个正面因素。再说一次，这些只是我们团队现在在海外关注的几个主题，也是他们对国际股票仍保有确信的缘由。

turns.en: One thing that I think is interesting, a lot of investors, and I would say me included, believe that international stocks are largely a dollar play in the sense that dollar weakness typically bodes well for international stocks.
turns.zh: 有一点我觉得很有意思，很多投资者——我想把我自己也算进去——认为国际股票在很大程度上是一个美元的戏法，意思是美元走弱通常对国际股票有利。

turns.en: Do you have any thoughts on that? And, you know, especially given that this is a 50% hedge international ETF. Yeah. I mean, that's what we saw last year.
turns.zh: 你对此有什么想法？尤其是考虑到这是一只有 50% 对冲的国际 ETF。嗯，我们去年看到的正是如此。

turns.en: You know, international returns were very strong and partly because you saw that decrease in, you know, that a D the dollar really decreasing in value, uh, by 10%, uh, that had a lot to do with the returns, uh, in international.
turns.zh: 国际回报非常强劲，部分原因是你看到美元真的在贬值，跌了 10%，这对国际市场的回报有很大影响。

turns.en: Um, but again, you know, since then we've seen kind of a little bit of a reversal there and it's been very, you know, kind of hard to predict, which is why kind of that 50% might be a good way to go.
turns.zh: 但再说一次，从那以后我们看到有点反转，而且它非常难以预测，这就是为什么那个 50% 也许是个不错的走法。

turns.en: Going back to sort of portfolio application for international stocks overall and certainly HFXI specifically, a question that I've asked a lot of guests recently, and I'd absolutely love to hear your take on this, is that, uh, my sense is a lot of investors and advisors are underway international exposure in general.
turns.zh: 回到国际股票整体、当然也包括 HFXI 的组合应用层面。最近我问过很多嘉宾的一个问题，我也非常想听听你的看法。我的感觉是，很多投资者和顾问在国际敞口上一直落在后面。

turns.en: And I think everybody knows a story here. It's well documented, which is that US stocks have outperformed for so long and by so much that I think some people just, they threw up their hands and gave up on international stocks.
turns.zh: 我想每个人都知道这里的故事。这已经被充分记录：美国股票跑赢了太久、幅度太大，我觉得有些人干脆举双手放弃了国际股票。

turns.en: And then I would say the other piece of that, which is also well documented, is that investors tend to have a home bias, uh, anyways, right?
turns.zh: 然后我认为还有另一个同样被充分记录的方面，就是投资者本来就倾向于有本土偏好（home bias），对吧？

turns.en: US investors tend to be overweight US stocks, regardless of performance. And so two, two questions for you here. Um, number one, do you agree US investors are currently underweight international right now?
turns.zh: 美国投资者倾向于超配美国股票，不管业绩如何。所以这里我有两个问题给你。第一，你是否同意美国投资者现在在国际上低配？

turns.en: And then two, if so, what would be your words of wisdom on changing that? Like, is it a simple message of diversification? Right. I have absolutely seen that.
turns.zh: 第二，如果是，关于改变这一点你有什么金玉良言？就是一个简单的分散化（diversification）的信息吗？是的，我绝对看到过这种情况。

turns.en: I've seen many advisor matrices even, um, and it's definitely true that US investors haven't structurally underweight to international. It's only gotten worse as US markets have grown and become even more concentrated.
turns.zh: 我看到过很多顾问的调查数据，显然属实的是，美国投资者结构上一直对国际低配。而且随着美国市场的增长并变得更加集中，情况只是更糟了。

turns.en: Um, you know, if we look, for example, at the MSCI equity index, the proportion of US market cap versus international has grown tremendously.
turns.zh: 比如如果我们看 MSCI 股票指数，美国市值相对于国际的比重已经增长得非常多。

turns.en: Um, so if you're using that as your benchmark, naturally, many investors have continued to be overweight to the US. So for example, in 2014, it was like, like a 50-50 weight of US versus international.
turns.zh: 所以如果你拿它当基准，自然很多投资者会持续超配美国。举例来说，2014 年时美国对国际大概是 50-50 的权重。

turns.en: Now the US is over 60% of global market cap. Um, so not surprisingly, that investors have continued to be overweight to the US. But yeah, in terms of, you know, does it make sense to increase international?
turns.zh: 现在美国占全球市值超过 60%。所以并不奇怪，投资者持续超配美国。但说到，增加国际敞口是否合理？

turns.en: I mean, obviously diversification is always key. I know so many people talk about it, but you know, countries go through, uh, different market cycles, obviously, depending on what their economies are going through, monetary policy, fiscal policy, et cetera.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，显然分散化一直是关键。我知道很多人都在谈它，但不同国家会经历不同的市场周期，这取决于它们的经济状况、货币政策、财政政策等等。

turns.en: Uh, so diversification across regions is definitely important. Um, the other thing to keep in mind is sector diversification specifically. So, um, obviously the sector composition between US and, you know, international is quite different.
turns.zh: 所以跨区域分散肯定重要。另一点要记住的是行业分散。显然美国和國際之间的行业构成差别很大。

turns.en: So for international, you have more exposure to like financials and industrials instead of obviously in the US, we're very top heavy, uh, in tech.
turns.zh: 所以在国际这边，你有更多像金融和工业这样的敞口，而在美国，我们显然在科技上非常头部集中。

turns.en: Um, so you, you're able to diversify there as well. Do you think it's going to take longer sustained outperformance by international to, to get investors and advisors to sort of change their mind here on this?
turns.zh: 所以你也能在那里实现分散。你觉得需要国际资产更长时间持续的跑赢，才能让投资者和顾问在这件事上改变想法吗？

turns.en: Or do you, are you already seeing that? Like again, in conversations that you're, you're having, you know, what are you hearing or do you feel like people are starting to get their head around?
turns.zh: 还是说你已经在看到这种变化了？在你进行的对话中，你听到了什么，或者你觉得人们开始想明白这件事了吗？

turns.en: I know there's been a lot of concerns just around the top heaviness of US market cap weighted indices and into your point, it's very heavy on tech.
turns.zh: 我知道围绕美国市值加权指数那种头部集中已经有很多担忧，正如你所说，它非常偏重科技。

turns.en: So are you seeing more investors and advisors look to that diversification play and then what role does performance play in that? I think a lot of investors are looking elsewhere just because like you're saying there is that over concentration.
turns.zh: 所以你是否看到更多投资者和顾问在寻找那种分散化的机会？那么业绩在其中扮演什么角色？我想很多投资者正在把目光投向别处，就像你说的，因为存在那种过度集中。

turns.en: So they're looking at other areas of the market, even, you know, mid small caps within the US international other areas, um, they're absolutely doing that.
turns.zh: 所以他们在看市场的其他领域，甚至美国的中小盘、国际以及其他领域，他们确实在这么做。

turns.en: Well, Maria, uh, really enjoyed connecting this week. Again, when I saw HFXI and it crossed over $2 billion in assets and then I looked at flows, it just jumped off the page to me.
turns.zh: Maria，我真的很高兴这周能和你连线。当我看到 HFXI 跨过 20 亿美元资产，然后又去看了资金流，它就直接从我眼前跳了出来。

turns.en: So I wanted to get the story behind that. And so I appreciate you providing that. And thank you for joining me. Thank you so much. That was Maria Ronnie, senior director, equities product manager with New York Life Investments.
turns.zh: 所以我想了解背后的故事。谢谢你跟我讲这些，也感谢你来到节目。非常感谢。刚才这位是 Maria Ronnie，New York Life Investments 的董事总经理兼股票产品经理。

turns.en: Navigating the ETF market, get the precise data and analytics that smart investors rely on, build a stronger portfolio today at etfdb.com. I'm now joined by Sandra Tastani, head of global ETF product and strategy at American Century, who currently offers 49 ETFs, nearly $160 billion in assets.
turns.zh: 在 ETF 市场中穿行，获取聪明投资者依赖的精准数据与分析，今天就到 etfdb.com 打造更稳健的组合。现在加入我的是 Sandra Testani，American Century 全球 ETF 产品与策略主管，他们目前提供 49 只 ETF，资产接近 1,600 亿美元。

turns.en: That's across both American Century branded ETFs and the Avantus ETF lineup. And just this year, they've seen about $40 billion in inflows all together.
turns.zh: 这涵盖 American Century 品牌 ETF 和 Avantus 的 ETF 产品线。仅今年一年，它们合计已经录得约 400 亿美元的流入。

turns.en: $40 billion. It's been an excellent year for American Century. And Sandra is now joining me from New York. Sandra, it is a great to connect and welcome to the podcast.
turns.zh: 400 亿美元。对 American Century 来说是极好的一年。Sandra 现在在纽约与我连线。Sandra，很高兴连上你，欢迎上节目。

turns.en: Thank you so much for having me, Nate. It's good to see you. All right. So we are going to do a little tour through the financial markets this week.
turns.zh: 非常感谢邀请，Nate，很高兴见到你。好，这周我们要沿着金融市场小转一圈。

turns.en: And obviously highlight several American Century ETFs along the way. But before we do that, I just mentioned this growth of the lineup overall.
turns.zh: 途中显然也会重点介绍几只 American Century 的 ETF。但在那之前，我刚提到他们整条产品线的这个增长。

turns.en: And so I would love to start by having you offer sort of a state of the union on American Century ETFs. What's been going on this year? How is the firm position within the ETF space?
turns.zh: 所以我想先请你给 American Century 的 ETF 做一个'国情咨文'式的盘点。今年都发生了什么？公司在这个 ETF 领域的位置如何？

turns.en: What's keeping you busy right now? Yeah, happy to provide a state of the union. It has been a very strong year. We're obviously, you know, very pleased and grateful to all the investors who have faith in the strategies that we've been bringing to the table.
turns.zh: 现在有什么让你在忙？嗯，很高兴提供这份'国情咨文'。这是非常强劲的一年。我们显然非常高兴，也很感激所有对我们一直在推出的那些策略有信心的投资者。

turns.en: But, you know, as a firm, this has been a commitment for us now going almost nine years. So we launched our first ETFs in January of 2018. And if you can believe it, at the time, the entirety of the active ETF universe at that time was fifty billion dollars with a B.
turns.zh: 但作为一个公司，这件事我们投入已经将近 9 年。我们在 2018 年 1 月推出了第一批 ETF。如果你敢信的话，当时整个主动 ETF 市场的规模只有 500 亿美元——是带 B 的 50。

turns.en: And, you know, we we had a belief that, you know, if we were going to sort of harness investment capabilities that we had in house, those from like long standing investment strategies, as well as newer capabilities that we developed over time, most notably, of course, the avanta strategies that you mentioned that, you know, within a tax efficient cost effective wrapper that these active solutions would be would be
turns.zh: 我们相信，如果能把我们内部的投资能力利用起来——既有那些久经考验的投资策略，也有我们这些年逐步建立的新能力，最显著的就是你提到的 Avantus 策略——把它们放进一个节税、低成本的外壳（wrapper）里，这些主动解决方案会

turns.en: of a benefit to clients. And thus far, it's played out probably more so better than what we would have imagined. I think the entirety of the active ETF marketplace today is over two trillion dollars in assets where we're proud to say that we are the fourth largest issuer of active ETFs in the US.
turns.zh: 对客户是有益的。而到目前为止，结果可能比我们能想象的还要好。我想今天整个主动 ETF 市场的资产已经超过 2 万亿美元，我们很自豪地说，自己是美国第四大主动 ETF 发行方。

turns.en: It's been a big focus for us, but we do offer strategies and two brands, like you said, Nate. So, you know, we're in market with the American Century Strategies.
turns.zh: 这一直是我们的重心，但正如你说的 Nate，我们的策略分属两个品牌。所以我们在市场上有 American Century 品牌的策略。

turns.en: Those are strategies that really are looking to sort of be a brand extension of the fundamental research philosophies that we have offered to investors, you know, notably through mutual funds for 60 plus years.
turns.zh: 那些策略其实是想成为我们 60 多年来通过共同基金向投资者提供的那套基本面研究哲学的品牌延伸。

turns.en: And then within the avantas investors brand, that was a capability that was established in 2019 at really specifically the focus on low cost value added solutions to try to offer the flexibility of active management and the perceived advantages of indexing diversification, tax efficiency, cost effectiveness and between the two, like you said, we're just knocking on the door of 160 billion dollars of assets.
turns.zh: 然后在 Avantus Investors 品牌里，那是 2019 年建立的一项能力，专门聚焦低成本、有附加值的解决方案，试图既提供主动管理的灵活性，也提供指数化那些公认的优势——分散化、节税、成本效益。而这两个品牌加起来，就像你说的，我们已经快摸到 1,600 亿美元资产的门槛。

turns.en: So pretty, pretty incredible. Yeah, and I mentioned the flows just to share that nearly 40 billion dollars in inflows, which is remarkable. What do you attribute that to?
turns.zh: 那真是相当惊人。是，我提到资金流是想说，接近 400 亿美元的流入，这很不简单。你觉得这归功于什么？

turns.en: Why do you think the American Century ETFs and the avantas ETFs are resonating with investors and advisors? Yeah, I mean, we have really developed over the last eight, nine years a very broad offering, but with a focus on strategies that we believe play significant roles within advisor portfolios, right?
turns.zh: 你为什么认为 American Century 的 ETF 和 Avantus 的 ETF 能在投资者和顾问中引起共鸣？嗯，过去八年、九年里我们确实建立起非常广的产品供给，但重点是那些我们认为在顾问组合中扮演重要角色的策略，对吧？

turns.en: So we're looking to build strategies that can represent building blocks and be fairly easily incorporated into those types of problems that advisors are looking to solve for.
turns.zh: 所以我们想做的是能够充当'积木'（building blocks）的策略，能够相当容易地嵌入顾问想要解决的那类问题里。

turns.en: And that's worked well. We're not really known for or really, I would say, participating in a lot of the shiny toy kind of conversations that happen a lot in the ETF business, but that's okay.
turns.zh: 而这效果不错。我们并不是以参与 ETF 行业里很多那种'闪亮玩具'式的话题而出名，我也不觉得我们在这方面投入很多，但没关系。

turns.en: It's not really who we are. And I think if, you know, the sort of staying true to our history and our legacy and our core competencies has worked well.
turns.zh: 那不是我们的本色。我想，忠于我们的历史、传承和核心能力，这条路走得挺好。

turns.en: But, you know, related to that point, I think what's interesting is that, you know, when you do have a very broad offering across asset classes, geographies, investment styles, investment approaches, you can have conversations that go in a lot of different directions.
turns.zh: 不过，与这一点相关的，我觉得有意思的是，当你在资产类别、地域、投资风格、投资方法上都有很宽的产品供给时，对话就可能往很多不同的方向展开。

turns.en: But, you know, this market environment kind of lends itself to having people with pretty diverse points of view as to the, you know, current state of the union, the direction of the markets, et cetera.
turns.zh: 而眼下的市场环境，也天然让人们对于当前的状况、市场的方向等等有很不一样的看法。

turns.en: And so I guess if I had to sort of bucket conversations recently in the year to date period and, you know, sort of flows would speak to this, I think they would probably fall into two very broad categories.
turns.zh: 所以，如果要把今年以来的对话分个类，资金流其实也能说明问题，我觉得大概会落在两个很宽的类别里。

turns.en: And the first is like a, you know, how do I maybe finally, maybe for the first time in some time, look to diversify and make sure that I have the appropriate diversification within my equity allocation.
turns.zh: 第一个是：我该怎么也许终于、也许多年来第一次去做分散化，确保我的股票配置里有合适的分散程度。

turns.en: And that, you know, can take many forms. And then, you know, second one that's probably not surprising, even given this morning's news, like how to navigate very uncertain, fixed-income landscapes that we're facing today.
turns.zh: 这可以有多种形式。第二个大概不令人意外，即便看看今天早上的新闻也知道：如何穿越我们今天面对的这个非常不确定的固定收益版图。

turns.en: Well, you are giving me the absolutely perfect segue here because we're going to get into the financial markets, do a little tour here. And you mentioned the breadth of the American Century TF lineup.
turns.zh: 你给了我一个绝佳的过渡，因为我们接下来就要进金融市场转一圈。你也提到了 American Century 产品线的广度。

turns.en: Overall, that'll give us an opportunity to highlight a few of those ETFs along the way and maybe talk about how they're differentiated. And just in general, Sandra, I'm very interested to hear how you're viewing the financial markets because you do sit in the unique perch there and there is a lot going on.
turns.zh: 整体上，这会让我们有机会沿途重点介绍几只 ETF，也聊聊它们的差异在哪里。总的来说，Sandra，我很想听你如何看待金融市场，因为你确实坐在一个独特的位置上，而现在发生了太多事情。

turns.en: And so let's maybe do this. We'll go through U.S. equities, international equities and fixed-income. And let's start on the U.S. equity side where, as you know, it's been a strong year overall.

turns.en: S&P 500 is up 13 percent. Artificial intelligence obviously continues to be the biggest story in the markets that's dominating, you know, the headlines and themes.
turns.zh: 标普 500 上涨 13%。人工智能显然仍是市场上最大的故事，主导着头条和主题。

turns.en: How are you viewing everything right now as you look at U.S. stocks? Like what most has your attention? Yeah, I think that a lot of the conversations today focus in some way, shape, or form around the exposure to technology, to AI, to semiconductors, you know, to momentum perhaps.
turns.zh: 你看着美国股票时，现在怎么看这一切？什么最吸引你的注意？嗯，我想今天的很多对话都以某种形式围绕对科技、对 AI、对半导体，也许还有对动量（momentum）的敞口。

turns.en: And, you know, the sort of flip side of that is around, you know, the concentration that we're experiencing within the U.S. equity markets and within, you know, many of the broad indexes that represent, you know, either the actual portfolio through the passive ETF investments or, you know, the benchmark that managers are being sort of held to.
turns.zh: 而它的另一面，是我们正在美国股票市场、在很多宽基指数里经历的集中度——这些指数要么通过被动 ETF 投资构成了实际的组合，要么成了管理人被要求对标的那个基准。

turns.en: And so, you know, I think it's hard to say when U.S. equities are up 13 percent after, you know, several strong years that, you know, this is a bad environment.
turns.zh: 所以，当美国股票在好几年强劲表现之后又涨了 13%，很难说这是一个糟糕的环境。

turns.en: But, you know, the fact that 10 stocks represent 40 percent of the S&P 500 index or 10 stocks represent 60 percent of the Russell 1000 growth, it's got some people concerned.

And I think, you know, investors have learned and unlearned and learned again in recent weeks that, you know, multiples can contract and that can have the impact in portfolios, right?
turns.zh: 是的，盈利总体上是有支撑的，但有些地方的估值倍数也很强，所以估值可能是偏高的。我想最近几周投资者学了又忘、然后又重新学到：倍数是会收缩的，而这会反映在组合上，对吧？

turns.en: So, you know, I think one of the things that we're talking about a lot is in the growth space, how to think about a growth allocation, you know, for investors who don't want to take on a lot of tracking error, they maybe have a sort of Russell 1000 growth type of exposure in their portfolio or, you know, NASDAQ type of portfolio, exposure in a portfolio.
turns.zh: 所以，我想我们经常讨论的事情之一是在成长这块：对于一个不想承担太高跟踪误差（tracking error）、组合里大概是罗素 1000 成长那种敞口、或者纳斯达克那种组合敞口的投资者，该怎么看待成长配置。

turns.en: And kind of a contrarian idea for those conversations is around a portfolio that keeps you in growth, but does it in a way that is much more diversified in the percent allocation weight in individual positions, right?
turns.zh: 而这些对话里一个有点逆向的思路是：有一个组合仍然让你留在成长里，但在个股权重和配置比例上分散得多，对吧？

turns.en: So, we have a quality growth strategy, QGRO, that, you know, when five or six stocks, like a MAG-7 type of run are really strong, has a hard time holding up because it maintains a three and a half percent position cap on individual securities.
turns.zh: 所以我们有一只质量成长（quality growth）策略，代码 QGRO，当像 MAG-7 那样五只、六只股票猛涨的时候，它很难跟上，因为它对单个证券维持 3.5% 的仓位上限。

turns.en: But because of that, it does have that sort of diversifying effect when you start to see markets broaden out a bit. turns.en: the large cap stocks in the U.S. And we, I think, have a very, you know, a premier franchise within small caps within the Avantus investors offering that we have, both on the U.S. side in value, in core, also in international small caps, sort of underrepresented in a lot of portfolios. turns.zh: 美国大盘股。我想在我们 Avantus Investors 的产品里，有一个非常顶尖的小盘业务线，既包括美国的价值和核心（core），也包括国际小盘——后者在很多组合里配置不足。但这也许是另一个没那么知名的思路。我不敢说 ETF 市场上还存在空白地带（white space）。

turns.en: Probably doesn't exist. But in fundamentally driven, active, gross small cap, we sort of identified that this was a space last year. turns.zh: 大概是不存在了。但在基本面驱动的主动小盘成长这个领域，我们去年认定这是一个可以做的方向，于是带着一个策略进入市场，它利用了我们 30 多年投资小盘成长的积累。我们推了一只叫 Small Cap Growth Insights 的策略，成立不到一年，但表现很好，基本上实现了我们为它设定的投资目标。

turns.en: We think we've tackled sort of the capacity constraints around these types of strategies with the way we built it. And that's kind of an interesting one, because there's really not a lot available for investors. This is admittedly a cliche question, but I'm curious, you know, how do you
turns.zh: 我们认为自己的构建方式解决了这类策略常见的容量约束。这一点挺有意思，因为投资者其实没什么可选项。今天如果你想用 ETF 搭一块纯粹的小盘成长风格积木，能选的基本都是指数化策略，而在那些领域这会是个问题。这显然是个老掉牙的问题，但我很好奇你怎么

But you clearly have a lot of investors and advisors who say,
turns.zh: 看待主动对被动这个选择，尤其是在小盘股这样的领域——如果你看业绩记录，小盘上主动的表现远好于大盘混合（large cap blend）。那你怎么框定这个主动还是被动的决定？显然 American Century 的 ETF 更偏主动，不管更系统性还是更传统，你们都有这些选项。但你显然也有很多投资者和顾问会说：

turns.en: I'm just going passive, no matter what. So talk a little bit about that. Yeah, we do come across advisors who say passive no matter what. But I do think it's pretty rare, Nate. I think most advisors, when they're thinking about building, you know, a well-thought-out, sort of long-lived strategic allocation for investors to meet their goals, whatever, you know, that their investors may have, they're looking for what is the investment philosophy?
turns.zh: 我就是要被动，无论如何。所以聊聊这个吧。嗯，我们确实会遇到说不问情由只做被动的顾问，但我认为这相当罕见，Nate。我想大多数顾问在为投资者构建一个深思熟虑、可以长期持有的战略配置、以实现投资者可能有的任何目标时，他们要看的是：投资哲学是什么？

turns.en: Do I, does it align with how I think about it? What's the cost? Is this going to be tax efficient? And do I think that by taking a fundamental view, I can add value? And to your point about, you know, in small caps in particular, in international, a lot of spaces, managers have been able to demonstrate pretty much across the board that this is an area where you can distinguish between companies that, you know, have the ability to really sort of excel. And there's a lot of names.
turns.zh: 它和我的思考方式是否一致？成本是多少？它是否节税？我是否相信通过基本面的视角能增加价值？正如你提到的，在小盘、在国际，很多领域管理人几乎已经全面证明了，在这里你可以区分出真正有能力表现卓越的公司，而且这样的名字很多。

turns.en: Some of them you just don't want to own. You just really don't want in your portfolio. So being discerning, you know, not just picking winners, but being discerning about what not to own is also, I think, an important part of an active portfolio.
turns.zh: 其中有些你就是不想持有，你真的不想让它进你的组合。所以有鉴别力——不只是挑出赢家，而是有鉴别力地决定不该持有什么——我认为这也是主动组合的重要一环。

turns.en: Okay. So we've been focusing on U.S. equities. turns.en: So if you asked me this question about 12 months ago, I probably would have a different answer. Many advisors had, you know, not quite thrown in the towel, but we're getting pretty close to where they're, what their views were. And, you know, I kind of grew up in a school of thought that, you know, we don't, we can't time markets. We don't know when various regions, geographies, styles are going to take place. So you want to sort of have your, your exposure, you want to
turns.zh: 如果你 12 个月前问我这个问题，我可能会给出不一样的回答。很多顾问虽然没有完全认输，但也已经很接近了，那是他们当时的看法。而我算是成长在这样一种思路里：我们无法择时，我们不知道各个区域、地域、风格什么时候会轮到，所以你要保持你的敞口，你要

And it's been challenging to sort of convince people that that was still the case of until, you know, recently, last year, we saw outperformance of international markets versus U.S. And that's continued. You know, despite pretty significant geopolitical headwinds, I think it's just that constant reminder that, you know, yes, in the terms of the global
turns.zh: 去再平衡，这就是我那种 Jason Zweig '吃你的西兰花'式的思路。要说服人们情况依然如此，一直到去年我们亲眼看到国际市场跑赢美国之前，都挺困难的，而且这种跑赢持续了下来。尽管有相当明显的地缘政治逆风，我觉得这正是一直在提醒我们：就全球

turns.en: Profit growth is broadening, so you're seeing improving earnings outside the U.S. And I think that just, you know, I think one of the most surprising data points in this space was one that I saw from Bank of America research earlier in the year, actually surveyed their high net worth investors and found that even though international stocks represent, you know, 30, 35% of the sort of AQUI index, only about 5% of the allocations were directed to international.
turns.zh: 盈利增长在扩散，所以你会看到美国之外的盈利在改善。我想这个领域里最让我意外的数据之一，是今年早些时候我从 Bank of America 的研究里看到的：他们实际调查了自己的高净值投资者，发现尽管国际股票在 ACWI 这类指数里占 30%、35%，但只有大约 5% 的配置投向了国际。

turns.en: So there's been, I think, also a rebalance that's been happening, too. So that's probably the other the other piece of that, that, you know, maybe, maybe that sort of throw in the towel got a little too far. Yeah, I completely agree. And I've talked about this numerous times. I think you're 100% right.
